{
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "asset_category",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
      "source_groundedness": 0.9,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Categorises the expense type (hardware/travel/cloud etc.), well grounded in short_description and ci. Useful to isolate travel rows for the query, but is more of a routing dimension than a decline signal; moderate leverage."
    },
    {
      "name": "expense_origin_method",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.75,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Manual vs automated vs procurement origin is a plausible decline signal (manual entries may face more scrutiny). Grounded in phrasings like 'Automated' or 'Procurement of'; the procurement_request vs manual distinction is somewhat inferred but reasonable."
    },
    {
      "name": "asset_action_type",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.5,
      "source_groundedness": 0.75,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Action taxonomy derivable from descriptions, but largely redundant with asset_category and expense_origin_method (e.g. registration_tracking tracks 'automated'). Modest new leverage."
    },
    {
      "name": "source_id_present",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
      "source_groundedness": 0.95,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Trivially derived boolean from existing source_id column; near-restatement of an original field, so low novelty. But missing source_id is a plausible decline signal, giving some usefulness. Fully grounded."
    },
    {
      "name": "processing_lag_bucket",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Buckets processed_date lag; 'not_processed' for nan is correct behaviour. Processing lag / not-yet-processed is a strong candidate signal for declines. Grounded in processed_date vs opened_at, though exact bucketing not fully verifiable from samples."
    },
    {
      "name": "submitting_department",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.3,
      "source_groundedness": 0.5,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Largely redundant with the original 'department' column. Values look questionable: hardware/cloud rows attributed to Customer_Support and Sales with no supporting text in samples, suggesting the department is not actually readable from the shown source text."
    },
    {
      "name": "vendor_brand",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.65,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Extracts brand from ci (Dell, AWS, Samsonite). Well grounded and gives a genuine grouping axis; vendor could correlate with non-standard/declined expenses."
    },
    {
      "name": "description_specificity",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.65,
      "source_groundedness": 0.75,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Distinguishes specific vs auto-generated vs placeholder descriptions, a reasonable proxy for scrutiny/decline risk. Grounded in description phrasing, though 'auto_generated_template' vs 'specific_model_named' boundary is judgment-based."
    },
    {
      "name": "is_non_standard_item",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Directly relevant: non-standard items are a classic decline trigger. However the derivation criteria are opaque and not clearly warranted by the sampled source text, lowering groundedness confidence."
    },
    {
      "name": "hardware_asset_subtype",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.45,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Reasonable subtype extraction (laptop/desktop) with correct NULL for non-hardware, but an AWS EC2 cloud service was labelled 'server' as a hardware subtype, a mislabel. Also tangential to a TRAVEL-expense decline query."
    }
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
  "source_groundedness": 0.75,
  "rationale": "The added columns provide several genuinely useful axes for predicting declines (origin method, processing lag, description specificity, non-standard flag, vendor), though a notable cluster is hardware-centric and tangential to the travel-expense focus of the query, and a few (source_id_present, submitting_department, asset_action_type) largely restate original columns or each other. Groundedness is generally sound with correct handling of missing values, but there are hallucination concerns: submitting_department values appear unsupported by the shown text, and a cloud service was mislabelled with a hardware 'server' subtype. Overall the set clears both necessary conditions moderately well."
}
